properties.value: Dependency inventory: hash.js is a crypto library dependency the build ships (declared in the lockfile). properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: secp256k1 and @noble/secp256k1 are the blockchain-curve signing libraries this Ethereum-protocol project ships (curve used for ECDSA recovery in Solidity contracts and their JS tooling). Classical, Shor-vulnerable; inherent to the EVM stack, replaceable only by an ecosystem-level migration.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.value: Transitive dependency shipping a weak legacy KDF in the build. The application never derives keys with it; it is present via the browserify crypto shim stack pulled in by build tooling. Changeable here by pruning the dependency chain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Test-scope weak randomness: an integration test uses Math.random() to synthesize a random 18-decimal value for staking NFT descriptor coverage. Not a production security path, but it is a real non-cryptographic PRNG use in the repo; recorded so the pattern is visible if tests ever generate security-sensitive fixtures.

Not an adversarial path (no attacker-controlled input reaches this), but the non-constant-time digest comparison is real; timing is irrelevant here, recorded for pattern completeness.

properties.value: Dependency inventory: scrypt-js 3.0.1 ships the scrypt KDF with the build (used by ethereum-cryptography tooling for keystores). No first-party scrypt call site found in application code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD ships with the build through @noble/ciphers 1.3.0 (and tweetnacl, which implements it natively). No first-party call site found in application code; available in the shipped image.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AE cipher available in the shipped tweetnacl bundle; no first-party use. Presence recorded as the dependency inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Key-management infrastructure for production Ethereum transaction signing: deploy, staking-update and v3-migration scripts sign transactions through this wrapper. The KMS key is an AWS-managed asymmetric ECC_SECP256K1 key — custody in the cloud control plane, observable here, replaceable only by AWS. The ECDSA secp256k1 signature itself is quantum-unsafe (Shor); PQ migration for this asset waits on AWS KMS offering a PQ sign spec, none exists today.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider inventory: tweetnacl (NaCl: X25519 key agreement, Ed25519 signatures, XSalsa20-Poly1305 AEAD, SHA-512) ships with the build as a declared dependency. Its primitives are quantum-vulnerable (X25519/Ed25519) but present regardless of first-party call sites.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PQ-safe hash library bundle shipping SHA-2, SHA-3/keccak, BLAKE2/3, ripemd160 etc. Available in the shipped build; the application reaches hashing through ethers/ethereum-cryptography rather than direct noble calls. Presence recorded as dependency inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider inventory: @noble/curves (secp256k1, P-256, ed25519, x25519, bls12-381, etc.) ships with the build. This is the project's elliptic-curve provider layer; observable here, replaceable only by swapping the library.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider inventory: @noble/ciphers (chacha20poly1305, aes-256-gcm, salsa) ships with the build. Available in the shipped image; no first-party call site found in application code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The AWS SDK client through which @nexusmutual/ethers-v6-aws-kms-signer reaches AWS KMS — the key-management infrastructure confirmed at ALG-89c5c4b8 (lib/aws-kms.js and the deploy/migration scripts). Key custody in the AWS control plane; supported key specs (ECC_SECP256K1 etc.) are AWS's to change.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt is the memory-hard KDF behind ethers keystore (Web3 secret storage) wallet encryption/decryption. PQ-safe KDF; parameters live inside the libraries, not at any first-party call site.
